label: B25-RX-CPU-OBSERVABILITY-BOARD-INTERACTION
title: Volatile-configure the T-020 SOF and prove BOOT/READY/PONG/echo with CPU-visible RX evidence
reads: docs/tasks/evidence/T-20260920-011.json and its task-owned programming/direct-terminal runners as templates only

authorization.user_statement: 好，我们继续，许可使用Quartus和JTAG来烧写和测试设备。直接使用这个命令行即可读取和交互。
authorization.authorized_scope: Configure the exact frozen T-020 SOF into FPGA volatile SRAM and use the direct JTAG-MPSSE terminal for bounded receive/transmit testing.
excluded: JIC/EPCQ/Flash write or erase and every persistent programming format
stopping the standard jtagserver, an unknown process or any pre-existing process

console.input_rule: Use one live direct terminal. Wait for READY and startup TX drain, then send each raw single character separately and wait for its response/diagnostic evidence before the next; do not substitute ordinary-file stdin or batch the four bytes.

scope: Preflight the golden-running board and exact SOF identity, configure only volatile FPGA SRAM using the task-owned 15 MHz programming server, attach the user-specified direct terminal immediately, and prove deterministic bidirectional firmware interaction plus three-layer RX observability. On functional failure only, restore the content-addressed golden SOF before release.

expected.status: Input '?' produces CLOCK25 plus current CAL and DDR state.
expected.debug: Input 'd' produces an immediate RXDBG line.
expected.echo: Input 'Z' produces exactly one target-side Z echo.
expected.hardware_path: RXPATH proves bridge, PoC and core dmem raw response words agree for the accepted bytes, including final 0xA45A, with counts advancing and fault clear.
expected.firmware_path: RXCPU proves four valid getc and dispatch events, final getc low16 0xA45A, final dispatch class=5/byte=0x5A, and successful putc/TX activity.

acceptance: The exact T-020 SOF configures successfully and one direct terminal session proves LCVEX25 BOOT, READY, CLOCK25 status, PONG, immediate debug response, printable Z echo, RXPATH bridge=PoC=dmem, and RXCPU getc/dispatch/putc/TX progression. Indirect bridge-only evidence is insufficient.

procedure.preflight: Under gamepc lock require exact candidate/golden identities, expected JTAG ID 0x02E060DD, no conflicting EDA/programmer/terminal or port-1310 listener, and identify/preserve the standard Quartus jtagserver (historically PID 5640) without assuming a stale PID is still live.
procedure.program: Clone only the known task-owned custom server files, verify their hashes and 15 MHz/channel-0 configuration, start one owned foreground server, run quartus_pgm for volatile SOF configuration, require configuration/operation success plus candidate checksum/JTAG ID, then stop only the recorded owned server PID.
procedure.interact: Run the exact direct nios2-terminal command, capture the complete first-session transcript, wait for READY/TX drain, and conduct the paced four-byte sequence in that same terminal.
procedure.finish: If full acceptance passes, stop only the task-owned terminal and leave the candidate running. If any functional acceptance item fails, stop only task-owned processes, restore the exact golden SOF by volatile configuration, and verify golden design identity/output before releasing the lock.

resource: Hold resource-lock gamepc across every remote/JTAG action and treat the cable as exclusive. Use event-driven monitoring with waits up to one hour; do not poll frequently.
forbidden_regions: JIC/EPCQ/Flash write or erase and all persistent formats
power cycle, board/SoC reset or physical manipulation
broad process-name termination or stopping the standard jtagserver, unknown or pre-existing processes
unverified SOF, cable, device, instance, checksum or JTAG ID substitution
synthesis, fitter, STA, assembler or tracked RTL/firmware/test changes

dispatch.monitoring: event-driven, up to one-hour waits, no frequent polling

result.candidate_programming: PASS; exact T-020 SOF, checksum 0x3159F8A0, JTAG ID 0x02E060DD
result.boot_ready: PASS; LCVEX25 BOOT, CAL-WAIT, DDR-FAIL, READY
result.hardware_path: PASS for '?'; bridge/PoC/dmem all 0x0000A43F, event counts 1/1/1, fault 0
result.firmware_path: FAIL; getc raw low16 0x0000 and dispatch class 0/byte 0, so CLOCK25 response absent
result.remaining_inputs: p/d/Z intentionally not sent after the first paced acceptance failure
result.safety: No JIC/EPCQ/Flash, reset or power action; standard jtagserver PID 5640 preserved; only task-owned processes stopped
result.next: Diagnose and repair response-data alignment between the observed core dmem response and the firmware-visible load/writeback value; add a failing regression before rebuilding the physical chain
